body:
Greg's words, VERBATIM, relayed by Fable2 (TermAl mailbox 4daa5b87 #6534, 2026-11-16T05:10Z) from Asistant #1890, at his request to pass them literally to authors:
„jaki znowu konflikt, znowu hipoteza, ktore bedzie zrobiona zle
i znowu sie wyjebie za pare godzin i bedziemy naprawiac tydzien

prosilem o proste procedury a nie procedury sprawdzajace wszystko!
WTF
przekaz doslownie autorom

sprawdzanie procesow NIE BEDZIE DZIALAC WIARYGODNIE"
(Gloss: "What conflict again, again a hypothesis that will be done wrong, and it will blow up again in a few hours and we'll be fixing it for a week. I asked for simple procedures, not procedures that check everything! WTF. Pass this literally to the authors. Checking processes WILL NOT WORK RELIABLY.")
Fable2's application for Opus2: no process-list or census steps in restart, install or landing procedures. The C6 restart census Fable2 had added is withdrawn (memory restart-one-way-backup-steps-2026-11-16). For Opus2's own install procedure this means: no FreeVirtual or process gate in the install, swap or landing steps; keep those procedures simple.

Clarification from Fable2 (TermAl #6536, 2026-11-16T05:11Z): Greg's rule targets PROCESS listing, census and snapshots used as steps or evidence. A free-memory floor before a cargo build is a resource guard, not a process check. Whether to keep it on the install build is the integration owner's call; keep it if dropping it risks an out-of-memory build failure on Central. So Opus2 KEEPS the FreeVirtual floor before Central cargo builds, including the install release build, and drops only process-list or snapshot steps from restart, install and landing procedures.
